name: Esoteric neo-Nazism
summary: Esoteric neo-Nazism fuses Hitlerism with occult and Indo-European religion. It treats Adolf Hitler as a divine figure or avatar, sees history as a decline from a golden age fought by an elite of Aryan 'men against Time', holds the Aryan race to be of higher and perhaps divine origin, and blames Jews and Freemasons for decay. Its leading writers also hold a nature religion that condemns cruelty to animals and refuse to condemn aggressive war.
scope: The Devi-Serrano strand: Savitri Devi (The Lightning and the Sun, The Impeachment of Man) and Miguel Serrano (Manu, The Resurrection of the Hero). Myatt and the Order of Nine Angles, and non-Nazi occultism, are excluded. Where these authors say nothing the answer is null.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Devi's 1958 book names the belief in the 'equal rights' of 'all men' among the most dangerous superstitions and calls the denial of the dogma of human equality the basis of an aristocratic conception of history (Part on Hitler, Lightning and the Sun).

hereditarian-race.rationale: Devi writes of a 'natural hierarchy of races' with the Aryan the noblest, and ties a person's duties and rights to caste as race; she gives no study of test scores, but the ranking of races by inborn quality is her stated premise.

racial-pride.rationale: The book presents the Aryan as the noblest race and treats preserving its racial aristocracy as the first duty; pride in one's own blood is the core of the creed in both Devi and Serrano (who speaks of the Aryan's lost 'pride' and 'divine origin').

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Devi names racial mixture as the primary cause of downfall and quotes the Bhagavad-Gita on 'confusion of races' with approval, crediting Hitler with the same view.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Devi praises the Hindu caste system, ordered by race and the Laws of Manu with their ideal of blood-purity, as better than liberal society; she does not set out segregation of housing, schools or facilities, so the answer is moderate.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Devi blames 'international Jewry' and Freemasonry for Europe's sinking and Germany's defeat, and Serrano writes of a Jewish Masonic brotherhood and world Jewish conspiracy behind wars and persecutions.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Devi states that whoever is not for the 'everlasting Forces of Light and Life' is against them, casting history and politics as a cosmic fight against decay; Serrano's Eternal Combat is the same.

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: Part I of Lightning and the Sun places the Golden Age at the beginning and sees history moving 'towards decay and dissolution', denying progress in the value of man; Serrano says the Golden Age inevitably falls to the Age of Iron.

return-to-pre-conversion-religion.rationale: Serrano says the Pagan Occident's development was cut off by Rome and Christianity and wants the Folk to return to Wotan and its own gods; Strube describes Devi's 'Aryan Paganism' opposed to Judeo-Christianity.

religion-from-peoples-character.rationale: Kaplan reports Devi's Norse and Vedic pantheons as a fitting Aryan racial religion, and Serrano roots his religion in the blood memory of the Aryan Folk.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Impeachment of Man calls for a 'natural human aristocracy' of supermen to rise and rule, and Lightning and the Sun rests on the rule of the natural elite of blood and character.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Devi hopes the lords of the age will render Hitler divine honours and calls him a god-like individual; Serrano dedicates his book to Hitler 'the Avatar'; both treat the leader as divine, though neither writes about heads of state in general.

leader-cult.rationale: Devi dedicates her book to Hitler as the godlike man against time and hopes for rites of divine honour; Serrano calls him the Avatar, a cult of the leader as the embodiment of the Aryan cause.

democracy-best.rationale: Devi calls 'individual freedom' and equality of opportunity the lying glories of modern Democracy and names equal rights among the dangerous superstitions; Serrano says immortality is 'neither democratic nor collective'.

revolution-justified.rationale: Devi holds that a bold minority fighting 'against Time' for Golden Age ideals must become ever more ruthless, and admits the necessity of ruthlessness in any revolutionary struggle.

political-violence-never.rationale: Devi dismisses 'squeamish pacifists' and defends ruthless violence in the service of the cause, while Impeachment of Man excuses 'acts of violence upon hostile human elements'.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Devi writes: 'We flatly refuse to condemn war, be it a thousand times a war of aggression', and her book defends the pursuit of living space by conquest.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Devi writes that the German people must be given living space according to their number and abilities, or conquer it where no valuable creation is spoilt, and calls this an accepted moral principle.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Serrano calls the Holocaust a farce and says there never were gas chambers; Devi's 1958 book says there was no planned extermination of Jews, and Kaplan calls her an early convert to Holocaust denial. Her 1946 text had accepted the reports, so the answer follows her later, sustained position.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The Impeachment of Man is a treatise on the rights of animals and plants, condemning vivisection, slaughterhouses, hunting and the fur trade as appalling cruelty.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Devi condemns the butchering of lambs, hunting and dissection of animals as cruelty that the man-centred faiths wrongly allow, and holds meat-eating wrong, so she rejects keeping animals for food or research even if humanely done.

humans-entitled-to-use-animals.rationale: The Impeachment of Man attacks the man-centred belief that creatures were appointed as meat and exploitable for man's enjoyment, and Lightning and the Sun rejects the idea of man's 'mastery' over Nature.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Devi's life-centred religion values animals and plants for their own sake, setting a dog above a degenerate man, as Kaplan summarises the book.

limit-population.rationale: Devi would stop the indiscriminate production of babies and encourage few or no births in overpopulated countries, especially of inferior racial stock; she is selective rather than general.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Devi would cease bribing people to have children in countries of moderate birthrate, except those of exceptionally fine racial stock, which opposes general family incentives.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Devi blames doctors who keep the weak and deficient alive and 'do nothing to prevent further such ones being born', and praises painless chloroforming of 'worthless human idiots'; she offers no programme for the state.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Devi holds that the noble races, the Aryan first of all, stand above others in a natural hierarchy, which contradicts the equality of cultures.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Devi quotes Hitler that the German people are 'no longer racially homogeneous' as a cause of decline and calls the belief in citizenship and culture over race a dangerous superstition.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Devi holds the German anti-Nazis guilty and calls the hanged Nuremberg leaders martyrs; she treats the post-war anti-Nazi order as the work of the forces of decay.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Devi calls the capitalists' system rotten and says the world loses nothing by its disappearance, yet holds that Marxism is the danger, and sees National Socialism as the only antidote.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Devi cites the National Socialist programme's recognition of private ownership only as the product of personal work, not speculation, and says even that could be swept away without catastrophe.
